title: Derived parent display statuses + Web UI status readability
summary: Introduce a parent-only derived display-status layer and improve Web UI readability with color/icon/pattern semantics.
description:
Current parent status derivation in `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts` is optimized for workflow rollup but does not always read clearly in the Web UI when a phase/feature has mixed child outcomes and no active child. Recent fixes already tightened one misleading case (`done + deferred -> deferred`), but the broader reading problem remains: parent entities need a display-oriented summary that communicates whether work is active now, started but idle, uniformly waiting/blocked/deferred, or fully closed with mixed terminal outcomes. The main affected UI surfaces are the Work Tree and dashboard rows in `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx`, reusable status/badge primitives in `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/ui/badges.tsx`, and entity detail/list surfaces that currently depend on a single status color to communicate state.

This phase should define and implement a parent-only derived display layer for `feature` and `phase`, keeping workflow statuses as the canonical operational model while introducing presentation semantics better suited for fast scanning. Locked direction from discussion: do NOT add `started` as a persisted workflow status alongside `in-progress`; instead, derive presentation statuses such as `started` and `closed` for parent entities only. `in-progress` should mean active child work exists now. `waiting`, `blocked`, and `deferred` should be surfaced directly only when the unfinished meaningful remainder is homogeneous. `closed` should summarize entities whose children are all terminal but with mixed outcomes such as `done/canceled/rejected`. Mixed non-active remainder that cannot honestly collapse to one specific workflow label should render as `started` in the display layer rather than overloading `planned` or `in-progress`.

The implementation should preserve the planner’s source-of-truth discipline: task/phase/feature canonical workflow state remains in the structured planner data, while display status, breakdown counts, and optional `hasStarted`/activity metadata are derived at read time or adapter/UI boundary. The Web UI must not rely on color alone; similar states should also differ via iconography, border/pattern treatment, and accessible tooltip/breakdown text. Behavior to preserve: task lifecycle semantics, existing planner data compatibility, current terminal statuses (`done`, `canceled`, `rejected`), and the ability to reason about parent rollups without making the core harness-specific.
goals: Define a parent-only derived display-status model that improves readability of `feature` and `phase` state in the Web UI without changing canonical task workflow semantics.
Specify precise rollup/display semantics for `in-progress`, `started`, `waiting`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `done`, `closed`, `canceled`, and `rejected` at parent level.
Expose enough derived metadata (for example breakdown counts and/or `hasStarted`) to let the UI explain mixed states instead of hiding them behind a single badge.
Update key Web UI surfaces so status readability comes from a combination of color, icon, border/pattern, and tooltip/popover breakdown rather than color alone.
nonGoals: Do not add `started` as a persisted workflow status editable by users on tasks.
Do not replace the planner JSON source of truth with UI-only ad-hoc state.
Do not make the core harness-specific or couple display semantics to Pi-only behavior.
Do not redesign every route in the Web UI during this phase; focus on status-bearing surfaces first.
dependencies: `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts` existing parent rollup logic and recent `done + deferred -> deferred` fix.
`packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/ui/badges.tsx` plus any existing shared status badge/token utilities.
Status-bearing detail/list/dashboard views introduced in earlier improvement phases such as P033(F005) and related UI polish phases.
risks: Confusing canonical workflow status with derived display status if naming and API shape are not explicit.
Status-history drift if derived display states are accidentally persisted or logged as canonical transitions.
UI inconsistency if some routes use canonical status colors while others use the new display layer.
Accessibility regressions if the design relies on hue alone without pattern/icon reinforcement or explanatory text.
openQuestions: Should derived display status be computed centrally in core/shared helpers and returned to clients, or should the Web UI compute it from child data using a shared imported utility?
Should filters/search operate on canonical workflow status, derived display status, or both?
Should `hasStarted` be a first-class derived field, or is `displayStatus + breakdown` sufficient for the first iteration?
decisions: Keep existing workflow statuses (`planned`, `in-progress`, `waiting`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `done`, `canceled`, `rejected`) as the canonical operational model.
Introduce `started` and `closed` only as parent-level derived presentation states, not as persisted workflow statuses.
Interpret `in-progress` at parent level as 'there is active child work now', not merely 'some work was done in the past'.
Surface `waiting`, `blocked`, and `deferred` directly only when the unfinished meaningful remainder is homogeneous; otherwise use `started` for mixed non-active remainder.
Represent fully terminal mixed outcomes (`done/canceled/rejected`) as `closed` in the display layer rather than overloading `done`.
Improve Web UI readability with combined color + icon + border/pattern + tooltip/popover breakdown, not color alone.

acceptedDecisions.title: Parent-only derived display status layer
acceptedDecisions.decision: `started` and `closed` will exist as derived presentation states for parent entities (`feature`, `phase`) rather than persisted workflow statuses.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: This preserves the clarity of the canonical workflow model while solving the Web UI readability problem where mixed child outcomes and non-active states are currently hard to scan.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Add shared derivation logic near existing rollup helpers; keep planner JSON/source-of-truth unchanged and feed the UI derived fields from shared code.

acceptedDecisions.title: Parent `in-progress` means active child work exists now
acceptedDecisions.decision: A parent should render `in-progress` only when at least one child is actively running (and optionally `discovery` where that concept applies), not just because some sibling child is already `done`.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The main goal is to improve readability: users scanning the Web UI should be able to trust that `in-progress` means active work, not historical partial completion.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Revisit parent derivation logic and/or add a display-layer derivation that separates active work from historical progress.

acceptedDecisions.title: Specific non-active states only when remainder is homogeneous
acceptedDecisions.decision: `waiting`, `blocked`, and `deferred` should be shown directly only when the unfinished meaningful remainder is homogeneous; mixed non-active remainder should display as `started`.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: This avoids lying with an overly specific label when the remaining child states actually point in different directions.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Treat `canceled` and `rejected` as terminal outcomes in the terminal/closed logic rather than as active unfinished remainder drivers.

acceptedDecisions.title: Web UI status readability uses multiple signals
acceptedDecisions.decision: Status rendering should use color, iconography, border/pattern treatment, and textual breakdown/tooltip support instead of color alone.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The problem being solved is primarily Web UI readability; multiple visual channels reduce ambiguity, improve accessibility, and help distinguish similar non-active states quickly.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Define a reusable display-status token mapping and apply it consistently across badges, tree rows, and detail/list headers.

completionCriteria: A shared specification exists for deriving parent display status and any supporting metadata such as breakdown counts or `hasStarted`.
The implementation preserves canonical workflow statuses and does not persist `started`/`closed` into planner source-of-truth fields.
At least the main Web UI status-bearing surfaces (Work Tree plus one additional shared badge/list/detail surface) render parent states using the new display layer consistently.
Mixed terminal parents such as `done + canceled` no longer present as plain `done`; they render as `closed` with an explanatory breakdown.
Visual differentiation between `started`, `in-progress`, `waiting`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `closed`, and terminal statuses is possible without relying only on color.

tasks.title: Core: display-status module + types + algorithm + truth-table tests
tasks.description:
Create a new harness-agnostic module `packages/plan-core/src/display-status.ts` that implements the parent-only derived display-status layer.

Requirements:
- Export `WorkflowStatus`, `DisplayStatus`, `StatusBreakdown`, `ParentDisplay` types as defined in the P039 spec.
- Export `countBreakdown(childStatuses)` helper.
- Export `deriveParentDisplay(childStatuses: WorkflowStatus[]): ParentDisplay` implementing the exact algorithm from the spec:
  1. if any meaningful child is active (`in-progress`, and `discovery` where applicable) → `in-progress`
  2. if all children are terminal (`done`/`canceled`/`rejected`): all `done` → `done`; all `canceled` → `canceled`; all `rejected` → `rejected`; otherwise → `closed`
  3. compute `unfinished = meaningful.filter(open)`; if homogeneous `waiting` → `waiting`; homogeneous `blocked` → `blocked`; homogeneous `deferred` → `deferred`
  4. if all unfinished are `planned` and `hasStarted === false` → `planned`
  5. fallback → `started`
- `hasStarted = meaningful.some(s => s !== "planned")` (at least one meaningful child is not planned).
- `meaningful = childStatuses.filter(s => s !== "canceled" && s !== "rejected")`.
- The function must be pure, non-persisting, and reusable by adapters and the Web UI.
- Export the module from `packages/plan-core/src/index.ts`.

Tests: create `packages/plan-core/test/display-status.test.mjs` with the full truth table:
- `done + planned` → `started`
- `done + waiting` → `waiting`
- `done + blocked` → `blocked`
- `done + deferred` → `deferred`
- `done + canceled` → `closed`
- `canceled + rejected` → `closed`
- `planned + planned` → `planned`
- `planned + waiting` → `started`
- `planned + blocked` → `started`
- `waiting + deferred` → `started`
- `blocked + deferred` → `started`
- `in-progress + done` → `in-progress`
- all `done` → `done`
- all `canceled` → `canceled`
- all `rejected` → `rejected`
- empty array → `planned` (or `draft` — confirm edge case in code)
- verify `breakdown` counts and `hasStarted` for representative cases.

Behaviors to preserve: do not mutate inputs; do not persist anything; keep the core harness-agnostic.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented the parent-only derived display-status layer in `@agent-plan/core`.

Delivered:
- New module `packages/plan-core/src/display-status.ts`:
  - Types: `WorkflowStatus`, `DisplayStatus` (adds parent-only `started` and `closed`), `StatusBreakdown`, `ParentDisplay`.
  - `countBreakdown(childStatuses)`: pure counts per canonical status.
  - `deriveParentDisplay(childStatuses)`: pure, non-persisting derivation implementing the locked P039 algorithm:
    1. any active meaningful child (`in-progress`) → `in-progress`
    2. all children terminal → `done` / `canceled` / `rejected` if homogeneous, else `closed`
    3. unfinished meaningful remainder homogeneous → `waiting` / `blocked` / `deferred`
    4. all unfinished `planned` and `hasStarted === false` → `planned`
    5. fallback → `started`
  - `hasStarted = meaningful.some(s => s !== "planned")`; `meaningful` excludes `canceled` and `rejected`.
  - `toWorkflowStatus(value)`: narrows strings to the workflow union (rejects unknown values like `discovery`).
  - `fromCanonicalStatus(status)`: maps phase-only statuses into the workflow union (`discovery → in-progress`, `draft → planned`).
- Exported the module from `packages/plan-core/src/index.ts`.
- Tests `packages/plan-core/test/display-status.test.mjs` (28 cases, all green):
  - full truth table (16 cases) from the spec
  - breakdown counts, `hasStarted` semantics, canceled-only children, done+canceled closed, input immutability
  - `countBreakdown`, `toWorkflowStatus`, `fromCanonicalStatus` helpers

Fix during implementation:
- Initial algorithm checked `meaningful.every(s => s === "done")` for the all-terminal branch, which incorrectly returned `done` for `done + canceled` (canceled excluded from meaningful). Corrected to `statuses.every(s => s === "done")` so mixed terminal outcomes correctly derive `closed`.

Validation:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/core build`
- `node --test packages/plan-core/test/display-status.test.mjs` → 28 pass, 0 fail
- `pnpm check` (monorepo typecheck) clean

Outcome: the display-status derivation is harness-agnostic, pure, non-persisting, and ready for PlanStore integration (next task 4X6SX) and Web UI consumption.

tasks.title: Web UI: display-status token mapping + CSS patterns/vars
tasks.description:
Create the visual token layer that maps `DisplayStatus` to color, icon, border/pattern, and tooltip semantics, so the Web UI does not rely on color alone.

Requirements:
- Create `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/display-status-tokens.ts` exporting a `DISPLAY_STATUS_TOKENS` map (and a `getDisplayToken(status)` helper) with:
  - `colorVar` (CSS custom property name, e.g. `--status-started`)
  - `icon` (symbol/component key)
  - `border` / `pattern` (CSS class suffix for dashed/hatch/stripe)
  - `tooltipExample` (string template)
- Add CSS custom properties and pattern classes to `packages/plan-web-ui/src/styles/base.css`:
  - `--status-planned`, `--status-started` (indigo), `--status-active` (orange), `--status-waiting` (amber), `--status-blocked` (red), `--status-deferred` (violet), `--status-done` (green), `--status-closed` (slate/teal), `--status-canceled` (gray), `--status-rejected` (rose)
  - pattern classes: `.status-pattern-dashed` (started), `.status-pattern-stripe` (closed), `.status-pattern-hatch` (canceled), `.status-pattern-crosshatch` (rejected), `.status-pulse` (in-progress)
- Patterns must be accessible (distinguishable without hue): use border style + background repeating-linear-gradient.
- Keep light/dark theme compatibility (use CSS vars, not hardcoded colors).

Reference mapping (from P039 spec):
- `planned` gray ○ solid light
- `started` indigo ◔ dashed border
- `in-progress` orange ▶ fill + pulse
- `waiting` amber ⏳ fill static
- `blocked` red ⛔ fill strong
- `deferred` violet ⏸ fill muted
- `done` green ✓ solid
- `closed` slate/teal ✓× stripe pattern
- `canceled` gray ⊘ diagonal hatch
- `rejected` rose ✕ cross-hatch

Behaviors to preserve: existing theme tokens and status colors must not break; this adds new tokens and pattern utilities only.

---
**Completion summary:**
Created the visual token layer mapping DisplayStatus to color, icon, border/pattern, and tooltip semantics.

Delivered:
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/styles/tokens.css`: added missing status color tokens (`--color-status-waiting` amber, `--color-status-deferred` violet, `--color-status-rejected` rose) that were referenced in base.css but never defined, plus the two new parent-only display status tokens (`--color-status-started` indigo, `--color-status-closed` slate/teal). All use the existing `@theme` block for Tailwind v4 integration.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/styles/base.css`: added `.status-started` and `.status-closed` color classes, plus accessible pattern classes that don't rely on hue alone:
  - `.status-pattern-dashed` (started — dashed border signals "begun but idle")
  - `.status-pattern-pulse` (in-progress — subtle box-shadow pulse)
  - `.status-pattern-stripe` (closed — 135deg repeating-linear-gradient)
  - `.status-pattern-hatch` (canceled — 45deg diagonal hatch)
  - `.status-pattern-crosshatch` (rejected — bidirectional 45deg/-45deg cross-hatch)
  - `prefers-reduced-motion` guard disables the pulse animation.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/display-status-tokens.ts`: new module exporting:
  - `DisplayStatus` type (mirrors @agent-plan/core locally to avoid adding a core dependency to the SPA bundle)
  - `DisplayStatusToken` interface (colorVar, icon, pattern, label, description)
  - `DISPLAY_STATUS_TOKENS` record mapping all 10 display statuses
  - `getDisplayToken(status)`, `patternClass(status)`, `statusColorClass(status)` helpers
  - `buildBreakdownLabel(status, breakdown)` — builds accessible aria-label/tooltips like "Started · 1 done · 2 planned · 1 waiting"

Design notes:
- `DisplayStatus` is defined locally rather than imported from `@agent-plan/core` to avoid pulling the core package into the Vite SPA bundle. The decision to compute derivation client-side (importing core) vs server-side (API returns displayStatus) is deferred to a later task.
- Existing theme tokens and status colors are not broken; this only adds new tokens and pattern utilities.

Validation:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/web-ui build` green
- `pnpm check` (monorepo typecheck) clean
- `scripts/copy-web-ui.sh` synced to pi-adapter + plan-server web-ui-dist

tasks.title: Web UI: Work Tree rows with displayStatus + breakdown tooltip for parents
tasks.description:
Apply the display layer to parent entities (features and phases) in the Work Tree so mixed/non-active parents read clearly.

Requirements:
- In `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree-rows.tsx`, for feature and phase rows:
  - compute `ParentDisplay` via `deriveParentDisplay(childStatuses)` imported from `@agent-plan/core` (or via a shared hook `use-dashboard-tree.ts` that already has the children).
  - render the parent badge using the new `DisplayStatusBadge` with `displayStatus` and `breakdown`.
  - tooltip/popover shows the breakdown (e.g. `Started · 1 done · 2 planned · 1 waiting`).
- Task rows (leaf) keep canonical workflow status but use the new token styling for consistency.
- Preserve the mobile column layout (badge → status → title) and the `shrink-0` fixes.

tasks.title: Validate refs and resolve targets before allocating numbers in create tools
tasks.description:
Add pre-write validation to feature_create, phase_create, and task_create in both adapters so invalid refs / missing targets are rejected BEFORE allocating numbers or writing files. Also protect allocSeqNumber and savePhase/saveFeature/saveTask from persisting non-UUID ids or orphan references. Include regression tests and run full build + check.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented pre-write validation in both adapters and the core to prevent creation of features/phases/tasks with invalid or orphan references.

Changes:
- Added `isUuid` helper to `@agent-plan/core/naming` and re-exported it.
- Added `validateResolvedTarget` helper to `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`.
- In all four create tools (`pi-adapter` and `plan-mcp` for both `task_create` and `phase_create`), the target ref is resolved, validated as a UUID, and reloaded from the store BEFORE any number allocation or write.
- Core already had: UUID regex on `PhaseSchema.featureId` and `TaskSchema.phaseId`, referential-integrity guards in `savePhase`/`updatePhase`, and a collision guard in `allocSeqNumber`. Updated `integrity-regression.test.mjs` to match the new strict behavior (legacy corrupt data is now written directly to disk in tests instead of via `savePhase`).
- Added `packages/plan-core/test/create-validation.test.mjs` with regression tests covering non-UUID featureId rejection, F00x ref canonicalization, and non-UUID phaseId rejection.

Validation:

- `@agent-plan/core`, `@agent-plan/mcp`, and `@agent-plan/pi-adapter` all build cleanly.
- Pre-existing `resume-flow.test.mjs` failure is unrelated and was failing before these changes.
